item.title: USS Washington to relieve USS Lincoln. And, Jared Kushner to meet with Netanyahu
item.description: The USS Washington is on its way to the Middle East to relieve the USS Lincoln amid concerns about conditions aboard. And, Jared Kushner is expected to meet with Prime Minister Netanyahu to move Gaza talks forward.
item.content:encoded:
The USS Washington is on its way to the Middle East to relieve the USS Lincoln amid concerns about conditions aboard. And, Jared Kushner is expected to meet with Prime Minister Netanyahu to move Gaza talks forward.

(Image credit: Handout Photo by the U.S. Navy)
item.dc:creator: Brittney Melton

item.title: At least 6 dead after Ukraine launches aerial attack on Russia
item.description: Ukraine launched one of its largest aerial attacks of the war on Russia, killing at least six people. How are Russians feeling as the war grinds on?

item.title: As war with Ukraine wages on, a look at life inside Russia
item.description: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer speaks with Nina Krushcheva, professor of international affairs at the New School, about the current geopolitical climate in Russia.

item.title: Trump orders Pentagon to scale back joint exercises with South Korea
item.description: President Trump explained the decision by saying South Korea had declined to help with the "denuclearization" of Iran and he cited his good relationship with North Korea's leader.

item.title: Kushner meets with Hamas on the Gaza road map ahead of talks with Netanyahu
item.description: Jared Kushner, President Trump's son-in-law, held a rare meeting with Hamas leadership Sunday in Egypt, in a new diplomatic effort to make progress in the stalled Gaza ceasefire.

item.title: A good – and bad – week for Italy's art police and museum security
item.description: On Friday, Italian police said they'd recovered three paintings stolen from a museum near the city of Parma. By Saturday night, thieves in Sicily had made off with four more masterpieces.

item.title: What really happened in Ceuta? Why we may never find out
item.description: Hundreds of migrants have again attempted to cross from Morocco into the Spanish territory of Ceuta. This time, Moroccan officials fended them off, raising new questions about the crossing of July 30.

item.title: Families of USS Lincoln crew say Trump should be 'ashamed' of conditions on board
item.description: President Trump said the USS Abraham Lincoln deployment is "not nearly long enough." A family member of a sailor on board that ship said those comments are shameful.

item.title: Jason Arday, Cambridge professor accused of plagiarism, is found dead
item.description: Arday was 37 when he became Cambridge's youngest Black professor in 2023. He was found unresponsive Friday at a home in southwest London.
